data.summary: F10 stops mainly due to part shortages (supplier shortfalls and AGV downtime/lateness) and recurring torque equipment faults, confirmed by line-stopping andon pulls and M-06 telemetry failures.

findings.claim: Part shortages are the largest stop driver at F10, with supplier_short on shift A at 23 incidents and 423.7 downtime_min, agv_down on shift A at 68 incidents and 247.1 downtime_min, and agv_late on shift A at 71 incidents and 109.9 downtime_min.
AGV-related shortages recur on shift B, with agv_down at 46 incidents and 86.4 downtime_min and agv_late at 55 incidents and 85.3 downtime_min.

Torque faults are a recurring secondary cause, including controller_fault on shift A at 26 incidents and 272.0 downtime_min and on shift B at 14 incidents and 179.7 downtime_min, plus repeated torque_out_of_range and socket_worn faults.

Andon pulls confirm missing_part and equipment stops the line, with all 157 missing_part pulls and all 131 equipment pulls marked stopped_line true, while all 90 quality_check pulls did not stop the line.
Machine telemetry for F10 machine M-06 shows 22 failures and 4 overstrain failures across 708 telemetry hours, supporting equipment-level faults as a stop cause.

data.recommendation: Prioritize AGV reliability and parts replenishment at F10, especially agv_down and agv_late events and supplier shortfalls, and inspect or recalibrate the F10 torque equipment such as M-06.
